title: Instruments of the orchestra
examples: Is the flute in the brass family?
What is the difference between woodwind and brass?

explain.say: The orchestra has four main families of instruments.
Strings instruments are played by drawing a bow across them.
Woodwind instruments are played by blowing air across or into them.
Brass instruments make sound by buzzing their lips into a mouthpiece.
Percussion instruments create sound by being hit or shaken.

draw.text: Percussion: Hit or shaken to sound

explain.say: When you hear a loud, exciting sound, it might be the brass section.

faq.q: Are all the instruments in the orchestra different?
faq.a: No, they are grouped into families like strings and woodwind. This helps musicians know what to expect.
asks: What are the main groups of instruments?

faq.q: Does the size of the instrument tell me which family it is?
faq.a: Not always, but generally, the family tells you how the sound is made. For example, the flute is always woodwind.
asks: How do I tell the families apart?
Is size related to the instrument family?

faq.q: Can a single instrument belong to more than one family?
faq.a: No, each instrument is generally classified into one main family for music. This helps musicians learn the correct techniques.

faq.q: What is the difference between a woodwind and a brass instrument?
faq.a: Woodwinds use air blown through tubes, while brass instruments use buzzing lips into a mouthpiece. The sound source is different.
asks: How do they make their sound?
What is the main difference in sound production?

faq.q: Do the percussion instruments always sound rhythmic?
faq.a: They can be rhythmic, but some percussion instruments can also play long, sustained notes. They add texture to the music.
asks: What role do they play besides rhythm?

facts: The string section includes instruments like the violin and the cello.
Woodwind instruments include the flute and the clarinet.
Brass instruments are played by buzzing the lips into a mouthpiece.
Percussion instruments are played by striking or shaking them.

quiz.say: The trumpet belongs to which instrument family?
quiz.why: The trumpet makes sound by buzzing the lips into a mouthpiece, which is the definition of the brass family.

wrong.0: Woodwinds use air blown across or into a tube, like the flute.
wrong.1: Percussion instruments are hit or shaken, like drums.
wrong.3: Strings are played by drawing a bow across the strings, not by buzzing lips.

quiz.say: Which instrument family includes the oboe and the flute?
quiz.why: Both the oboe and the flute are played by blowing air through a specific tube, placing them in the woodwind family.

wrong.0: Brass instruments require buzzing the lips into a mouthpiece.
wrong.1: Percussion instruments are designed to be hit or shaken.
wrong.3: Strings require a bow or plucking action to create sound.

quiz.say: If an instrument is struck with sticks, it is most likely from the:
quiz.why: Hitting or striking an instrument, such as timpani, is the defining action of the percussion family.

wrong.0: Brass instruments require the musician to buzz their lips.
wrong.2: Strings are usually played by bowing or plucking, not striking.
wrong.3: Woodwinds are played by blowing air into them.
